findings.message: setProjectManager reads the project row with `projectOf` without a row lock, then checks the 'already the PM' guard and fills `from`, the audit `before` and the event from that read before it updates. If two handovers run at the same time, both read the same manager. The second one writes over the first, and its audit and `ProjectManagerChanged.from` name a manager who was already replaced. Its 'already the PM' guard can also pass on stale data. Fix: in the service, read the project with `select … for update`. Keep the unlocked read for the card and the proposal. Add a two-session test.
findings.scenario: Maya is PM of CON. An Admin hands CON to Nimal while Maya hands it to Sahan. Both transactions read manager_user_id = Maya. Nimal commits first, then Sahan commits. The project ends with Sahan as PM, but the audit row says before = Maya, not Nimal. The event's from = Maya. Nimal's own handover is overwritten and no event records that he lost the project.

findings.message: `viewerForUser` returns null when the manager's account is not active (packages/auth/src/session.ts:100). `teamIn` then sets `manager: null`, and ManagerLine shows 'PM: nobody yet'. So 'this project has no PM' and 'the PM's account is deactivated' look the same. That hides a project that needs a new PM, the opposite of 'lead with what needs attention'. Fix: when manager_user_id is set but the lookup finds no active account, return a separate state, for example `{ userId, name: manager_name, inactive: true }`, and show it as needing attention.
findings.scenario: Project FLT has manager_user_id = Nimal, and Nimal's account is deactivated. The /delivery/p/FLT/team page shows 'PM: nobody yet'. The project still has manager_user_id set and nobody manages it.

findings.message: Nothing ends a standing allocation when the person leaves or the project closes. The monthly job writes month rows for every open `allocations.standing` row and never checks whether the person is still employed or whether the project is still active. Fix: (a) in `extendStanding`, skip or end any standing row whose person is no longer active/joining (through `listPeople` or `getPerson` on `@amax/hr/contracts`) or whose project is not in `listProjectRefs`; and (b) when HR records a leaver (`hr.person.left`), end that person's standing allocations from the month after they leave. Add a variant test covering a leaver, an archived project, and a still-active control.
findings.scenario: Dinesh is set to 50% on CON until further notice in 2026-10 and leaves on 2027-03-15 (record_leaver). Each run on the 1st (2027-04, 2027-05, …) still writes a 50% CON row 12 months ahead, so the grid, demand totals and get_project_team show a leaver allocated to CON for as long as the job runs. The same happens after CON is archived.

findings.message: joinedOn defaults to `new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)`, which is the UTC date and not the date in the entity's timezone. For a Sri Lanka or Australia entity, someone added early in the local morning gets yesterday as their join and employment start date.
findings.scenario: At 03:00 Sri Lanka time on 2026-11-16, a person is added with no join date. Their joined_on and employment starts_on are both recorded as 2026-11-15.

findings.message: The month rows and events the extend job writes are attributed to `"allocations.standing"`, a job name, and not to the person who set the allocation until further notice. Core rule 4 says every record says who did it: the person, or an agent acting for that person. The standing row already stores who set it (`updated_by`). Fix: pass `s.updated_by` (for example as `"allocations.standing for <updated_by>"`) as `by` in `fill` and in the event payload. Attribution can currently be reached indirectly through `standing_id`, but the event payload and `updated_by` name nobody.
findings.scenario: Maya sets Dinesh to 50% on CON until further notice. The 2027-10 row the job writes on 2026-11-01 has updated_by = 'allocations.standing', and its allocations.allocation.set event has by = 'allocations.standing'. Neither names Maya.

findings.message: `activeAccount` matches a name or an email and silently returns the first match ordered by name (`limit 1`). When two active accounts share a name, `proposeAllocate` names one of them in the "Add them to HR first" hint, picked arbitrarily. Return null, or an ambiguous result, when more than one account matches, as `resolvePerson` already does for HR names.
findings.scenario: Two active accounts are both named "Priya Jayasena" and neither has an HR record. "Add Priya Jayasena to CON" suggests adding whichever account sorts first, possibly with the wrong email.
